physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the sacral plexus, the dense web of nerves behind the lower belly that runs the slow work of taking the world in. Digestion, absorption, the soft conversion of what came from outside into what is now you. It is the body's nourishing centre, lower than the heart, lower than thought, and it never stops asking the same question. Is there enough. Will there be enough.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. The hum of not-enough lives in the gut before it lives in the mind. A small clench under the navel, an appetite that eats without being fed, a fullness that does not fill. People carry it for years and call it stress, or call it themselves. The walls the shadow builds are walls of the belly first. The room that gets smaller is a body that has stopped letting things in.

The climb out is bodily too, and it is softer than people expect. The clench loosens before the thought changes. Food tastes like something again. A meal eaten without watching the clock. The belly warms and the watching stands down a notch, and from there the giving the gift speaks of becomes possible, because a body that is being fed can finally feed something back. The code lives where you are being nourished right now, while you do other things.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to a single amino acid, Leucine, one of the small set the body cannot make for itself. It must come in from outside, taken at the table, broken down, before any of the rest can run.

Leucine is the body's signal to build. It is the chemistry that tells a cell to grow muscle, repair tissue, lay down something new where the old has worn through. Nothing in you renews without it. It is a fitting floor for a card about nourishment. The gate of being fed runs on a letter that is itself fed in.

There is a teaching in that, and it is the quiet answer to the shadow's whole question. The not-enough was never the truth of the body. The body was already arranged around receiving, already built to take what comes and turn it into more life. The card runs all the way down to this. A chemistry that knows how to be fed, and how to use what it is given to build the next thing the world will need.
